comments.value:
I recently was on Adrenaline 22.10.3, which was the latest driver at the time and happened to crash on specific worlds, like the one Surami mentioned. I was trying to join my friends in Solar Cabins, but kept crashing, either being thrown into SteamVR Home or HMD would freeze (I could still communicate in the world)
I figured it was the driver because it was one of the recent changes that took place and I had been to Solar Cabins the day before I had updated to 22.10.3. What I would see before crashing was the media player in Solar Cabins artifacting or corrupting. I'm not sure if it's part of the issue, but I thought I should mention it.
The issue doesn't happen when in Desktop mode on 22.10.3, and I no longer have any issues after reverting back to Adrenaline 22.5.1, even in VR. I use a Radeon 6950XT as my GPU and currently the recommended driver is 22.5.1 while the latest Adrenaline 22.11.1 shows up as an optional driver.
link to Solar Cabins:
https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_87701b58-ee11-4ac1-80a6-6663ea1ca9c8

@{61ef1d4720e9de78d3489832|full_name}: It is sadly related towards the media players, someone mentioned on another post someone put up (https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/video-players-seem-to-crash-vrchat-after-latest-update), it is and VRChat are aware of it and are trying to fix it, and it isn't really related towards them, it is the company that they use the media players from, and this is mainly because the quest has some features that are good on their end, I don't really know what it would but I can guess better cross-platform support. 
However, I would say wait for a full month, and I assume VRChat would fix it as they have done their crazy development on the game after those events, so they should focus on giving better support for AMD users as it is now a growing market, and people aren't buying these GPUs at this moment because of that reason, which are amazing value. Otherwise, we will have to wait again, or just go back to the 22.4.x/22.5.x drivers. I am staying at 22.11.1 (which still crashes) because I can now use  HEVC in virtual desktop, which makes my game perform so much better. 
Anyway, I hope this gives you better information, also please upvote that post I linked too, here it is again: https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/video-players-seem-to-crash-vrchat-after-latest-update

@{61aaa869ce67b5447b2ab6dd|full_name}: Update, since 11.2.1 has been released

i've also noticed the other thread has this issue marked it as complete, but I'm actually having issues with the video player after updating to 11.2.1.

I can actually stay in worlds now with the newest driver, but watching Chainsaw Man was so painful while it has a lot of stuttering and the picture turning completely grey.

Solar Cabins has this grey screen issue and also in Anime Haven, where I'm watching anime has it. I've actually went to VKet's Parareal Nagoya, which has a ton of videos (it was 760mb for a reason, all the videos part of the Disney+ trailers) and their videos work okay. I know this issue is related to streaming video, but I just want to put it out there that the issue is just still that.

I can stay in worlds without outright crashing so it's an improvement, hope this helps.

@{61ef1d4720e9de78d3489832|full_name}: yeah 

there are some areas that either vrc or AMD need to refine 

propbably the the latter because they must have fixed the first issue to begin with

details:
AMD driver 22.10.2, crashes only VRChat when it comes to some slightly intensive world's (example: https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_f6445b27-037d-4926-b51f-d79ada716b31). I have no idea if this is an issue on the AMDs side or your side, but we had a discussion on the Virtual Desktop server about it and someone mentioning more lenient to your side. However, I did notice that the game was crashing not even on the latest, I was seeing it with 22.8.1 - 22.9.2. 
I hope this gave you se information to understanding what's going on with AMD GPUs as they have just fixed pretty much most of the VR troubles and here comes another bad one. Even if you think it could be on AMDs side, it would be nice for your side to send information to AMD as it might give them a higher chance in fixing this bug.
I currently rn:
CPU- RYZEN 5 3600
RAM- 16GB 3200Mhz (8*2)
STORAGE - 1 TB M.2 
GPU - RX 6600XT
Also, clearing contact cache doesn't work. Plus, it just doesn't happen on that world only, there's a number few of them where it out right crashes my game. Plus, there isn't a unity failed loading screen either. It just just goes from playing, straight away to the steam vr scene.
title: VRChat crashing on my lastest version of GPU drivers
